title: The Neutral Verdict on Dad's Driving
one_liner: An independent on-road evaluation of an aging parent's driving that gives adult children a credentialed Green, Yellow or Red verdict, plus a graduated plan so nobody has to be the villain about the keys.
customer: Adult children aged 45-65 of drivers 75+ pay $349-449 per evaluation and $12 a month for monitoring. Later buyers are auto insurers, Medicare Advantage plans and long-term-care insurers.
problem: Taking away the keys is one of the most dreaded family confrontations. The parent hears loss of independence and the child becomes the villain. Doctors rarely intervene, DMV medical review is slow, and driver-rehab specialists have months-long waitlists. Families wait for a crash. AAA and AARP offer generic tips, not an individual, defensible verdict.
solution: Frame it as a safety tune-up and send a certified evaluator, an OT with driver-rehab credentials or trained retired instructors under OT supervision. They ride in the parent's own car on a standardized 45-minute route with scoring for gap judgment, lane keeping, hesitation and scanning, plus a brief cognitive screen. The report gives a Green, Yellow or Red verdict. Yellow means no night, highway or rush hour with a recheck in six months, optionally verified by connected-car data or a cheap OBD dongle with the parent's consent. Red comes with a transition kit of robotaxi and rideshare credits, grocery and pharmacy delivery, and a senior-center pass, so retirement feels like an upgrade. The evaluator is advisory only and DMV referral is optional.
why_now: The oldest baby boomers turn 80 in 2026. Robotaxis now operate commercially in a growing list of US metros, so a real off-ramp finally exists. Connected-car APIs make objective driving data possible with consent. Scarce driver-rehab specialists can be leveraged with standardized scoring and remote review.
revenue_model: $349-449 per evaluation, a $12 monthly monitoring subscription for Yellow-zone drivers, and referral or ride-credit margin on the transition kit. B2B per-evaluation contracts with insurers and Medicare Advantage plans that want fewer elder-driver claims.
non_obvious_insight: The product is a third party who absorbs the blame. Families are buying relational insurance, not a road test. The recurring money is in the Yellow zone, where a graduated restriction plan needs ongoing verification, which turns a one-off confrontation into a subscription.
first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 driver-rehab OTs in one metro, plus elder-law attorneys and geriatric care managers for referrals. Build the scoring sheet from published road-test protocols. Get liability coverage and a consent script. Run 10 evaluations at a $249 intro price. Recruit through caregiver-support groups and Facebook groups for adult children of aging parents. Publish anonymized case studies.

title: Billable Legacy Circles for Advance Care Planning
one_liner: Community 'legacy circles' where older adults tell their life stories and finish their advance directives, with a clinician in the room to bill the Medicare advance-care-planning visit.
customer: Medicare Advantage plans and ACOs chasing advance-care-planning quality measures (paying per completed and documented ACP), plus adults 60+ paying about $79-99 for the circle and a keepsake legacy book.
problem: The longevity industry sells more years but says nothing about what they are for, while the 65+ population is peaking and lonely. Advance care planning has had Medicare billing codes for years (99497/99498), yet few eligible people have one, because it is framed as paperwork about death and clinicians have no time. The meaning conversation people actually want is unbilled, and the billable one is avoided.
solution: A 4-session circle of 6-8 people in libraries, churches and senior centers covers values, life story (dignity-therapy style prompts) and what a good ending looks like. Each participant then has a 30-minute individual ACP visit with an NP or social worker under a billing clinician, who files the health-care proxy or POLST. AI transcription and editing produce a 'legacy book' or short video for family. Plans get documented ACPs and engagement data, and participants get a keepsake and a group of peers.
why_now: About 4M Americans turn 65 each year through 2027, so demand is at a peak. Advantage plans are under margin and Star-rating pressure and want cheap, measurable gap-closing. AI transcription and editing make personalized legacy artifacts cheap. Longevity and GLP-1 hype have surfaced the 'healthspan for what' question.
revenue_model: ACP visit billing (about $85-100 per 99497 under Medicare), per-completion fees from MA plans and ACOs, $79-99 participant fee for the circle and legacy book, and sponsorship by estate-planning and elder-law firms.
non_obvious_insight: Advance care planning fails because it is sold as death admin and done alone. Framed as a legacy-building group with a keepsake, participants pull themselves in. The billing code is the boring spine that lets a community and meaning program be paid by a health plan. The group covers the reflection, and the individual visit, not the group, is what gets billed.
first_30_days: Recruit one NP or LCSW (with a supervising physician) and two host venues, such as a public library and a church. Run three circles at $79 and produce sample legacy books. Take the results to the quality lead of one MA plan or ACO that publishes an ACP gap list. Confirm payer-specific billing rules with a compliance advisor before billing anything.

title: Caring Contacts as a Service for Hospitals
one_liner: Outsourced, human-edited follow-up messages and calls after a suicide-risk emergency visit or crisis call, run on a compliance-grade platform hospitals and 988 centers can buy per patient.
customer: Hospital EDs and behavioral units, state-funded 988 crisis centers, university counseling centers and behavioral-health carve-out plans, paying $40-120 per patient enrolled or $5-15k a month per site.
problem: The highest-risk window is the weeks after discharge or a crisis call. The Joint Commission's NPSG 15.01.01 requires follow-up policy, and randomized trials of brief, non-demanding 'caring contact' messages show fewer attempts. Yet most systems run this through one overwhelmed staffer mailing postcards, with no delivery guarantee, tracking or outcome reporting.
solution: A managed service: enrollment at discharge on a tablet, a cadence built from an evidence-based message library (days 1, 3, 7, 14, 30 and beyond), AI drafting with human review, two-way replies routed to trained staff, escalation with warm handoff to crisis lines, and EHR-connected dashboards for Joint Commission and Zero Suicide reporting.
why_now: 988 volume has grown since 2022, about a dozen states now levy 988 telecom fees that fund local centers, and the Harvard study estimating 4,400 fewer youth and young-adult suicide deaths in 988's first 2.5 years strengthens the funding case. 988 politics (Press 3 ended Jul 2025, a restored version excluding Trevor Project announced Jun 2026) push centers toward reliable, defensible operations.
revenue_model: Per-enrollee fee plus platform fee, funded by hospital quality budgets, state 988 funds and SAMHSA grants.
non_obvious_insight: The market chases AI that detects risk, but the best-evidenced and cheapest intervention is a human-sent, non-demanding note. The product is operations and proof (reliable delivery, documentation, outcome reporting), not detection.
first_30_days: Partner with one county crisis center and one hospital ED. Write the message library with a clinical advisor who knows the caring-contacts literature. Enroll 100 patients on a $10k pilot and measure re-contact and re-presentation rates.

title: Affordable Capital-Stack Solver for Conversion Developers
one_liner: A structuring engine and expert memo that tells first-time affordable developers which subsidy stack is fundable for a given office conversion, with a calendar of deadlines.
customer: Office owners, small and mid developers and nonprofits pursuing conversions on public land or under affordability mandates, and city housing agencies running RFPs.
problem: Conversions are moving to public land and affordable set-asides (NYC's 100 Gold Street grew to 4,000 units with 1,000 affordable). That drags market-rate developers into a 6-8 source stack (4% LIHTC and bonds, land lease, abatements, historic credits, PACE, city and state gap funds) with volume-cap timing and set-aside tradeoffs. Consultants charge $25-75K and take months, and deals die before they start.
solution: Input a building and city, and get the top three feasible stacks with set-aside options, equity pricing ranges, application calendar and funder checklists. A human affordable-housing finance specialist reviews each output and delivers a structuring memo; an add-on kit supports public-land RFP responses.
why_now: The 2025 federal tax law eased the bond test for 4% credits and raised 9% allocations starting 2026. Conversions increasingly require affordability, and distressed-office buyers need a plan quickly.
revenue_model: $8-20K flat structuring memo, a 0.5% success fee on closed subsidy, and $1.5K per month developer subscription.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input is not capital but a first-timer's knowledge of which stack is fundable and when. The winning product is an eligibility-and-calendar engine, not another architect's feasibility study.
first_30_days: Recruit two former affordable-housing finance directors. Publish stack templates for three cities with conversion incentives. Approach 20 office owners and receivers in those cities. Sell three memos at a $6K founder price.

title: Reverse Mzigo: Parents' Farm Feeds Nairobi Kids
one_liner: A weekly, consolidated truck route that moves food from rural parents' farms to their own adult children in Nairobi estates, paid by the children, turning an informal favour into a subscription that gives parents a dignified monthly income.
customer: Urban salaried Kenyans (25-45) who already receive 'mzigo' (parcels of maize flour, arrowroot, sweet potatoes, bananas, sukuma, eggs, kienyeji chicken) from their rural mothers. Suppliers are the mothers and other smallholders in their village cluster. Friends and neighbours of the children are the natural second wave of buyers.
problem: Farm-to-consumer startups keep dying on trust and customer acquisition: urban buyers do not trust unknown farmers and farmers do not trust unknown buyers. Yet a huge informal flow already exists in the opposite direction from the usual assumption: parents send food to their city children by matatu drivers and bus parcel counters, unreliably, unweighed, unrecorded, with spoilage and no payment trail. The children also quietly want to support their parents but handouts hurt parental pride and get 'shared' with relatives.
solution: Village-cluster pickup and Nairobi last-mile drops, organised by a WhatsApp group per village and a simple order cycle. The child orders or subscribes (say KES 2,000-4,000 per fortnight) and pays by M-Pesa. The parent gets paid the same day on delivery of graded, weighed produce at the village collection point. The platform handles packaging, a consolidated Saturday truck or van, cold-ish handling for chicken and eggs, and a photo receipt with 'from Mama Wanjiku' provenance. Buying food from mum becomes a socially acceptable remittance that preserves her dignity and creates predictable monthly income. Over time it adds friends-of-the-family boxes, bulk orders for church and workplace groups, and inputs credit for the mothers repaid out of box sales.
why_now: Urban food inflation and food-safety anxiety have pushed Nairobi professionals to look for known-source food. Mobile-money receipts and WhatsApp Business make the order-to-payment loop nearly free to run. Delivery infrastructure (van pooling, boda last-mile) is cheap enough in Nairobi estates to support a weekly consolidated route. Most Nairobi residents keep strong up-country ties, so the founder's own network is a zero-cost acquisition channel.
revenue_model: Delivery and platform margin of about 12-18% on box value (parents keep roughly 60-70%, transport and packaging the rest), plus a small subscription or priority-delivery fee. Later, inputs and micro-loan referrals to the mothers, and corporate or church bulk orders.
non_obvious_insight: The customer for rural produce is the farmer's own child, not a stranger. Family trust is a free, pre-built distribution network, and it removes the customer acquisition and trust costs that kill farm-to-fork startups. It also means the product is really a disguised remittance channel: paying for goods is a more comfortable way to support parents than sending cash.
first_30_days: Use your own parents' village and 10 neighbouring mothers, plus 40 Nairobi households from your WhatsApp contacts (school, church, workplace groups). Run one Saturday route on a hired pickup with a Google Form for orders and M-Pesa till for payment. Measure spoilage, on-time rate and how often children reorder, then add a second village once the unit economics on the first route are positive.

title: Birth Plan B for Maternity Deserts
one_liner: Carve the last three weeks of childbirth logistics out of the hospital: pre-booked lodging, ride dispatch, nurse triage and an emergency-delivery kit for mothers whose local labor ward closed.
customer: Payers: Medicaid managed-care plans and state programs spending Rural Health Transformation money, rural employers and self-insured plans, and mothers directly ($349 to $699). Users: pregnant women in maternity-desert counties.
problem: At least 96 hospital labor-and-delivery units closed across 35 states between 2024 and early 2026, and in nearly 60% of affected counties it was the only birthing facility. About one in three US counties is a maternity-care desert, and more Medicaid cuts starting in 2027 are expected to close more units. Families improvise the final weeks: a 60 to 90 minute drive, no place to stay at 39 weeks, a partner who cannot leave work, and unplanned roadside births.
solution: A subscription from week 34. It includes choosing and pre-registering a receiving hospital, plus a contracted hotel or extended-stay room within 15 minutes of that hospital, for the 38 to 41 week window or triggered at first contractions. It adds on-call ride dispatch through a local non-emergency medical transport or taxi operator, with backup childcare and pet care. A 24/7 OB-nurse triage line (a telehealth partner) decides between go now and wait. The kit includes emergency-birth supplies and a 45-minute partner class coordinated with local EMS, and it ends with a return ride and first-week check-ins. No clinical license is needed because it wraps logistics around existing care.
why_now: CMS awarded the $50B Rural Health Transformation Program to all 50 states on December 29, 2025 (about $200M per state in year one). 35 state applications include maternal or child health, several include obstetric transport, and states face an October 30, 2026 deadline to obligate first-year awards. That makes subcontractors with a concrete pilot unusually welcome right now.
revenue_model: A per-member-per-pregnancy fee of roughly $300 to $900 from Medicaid managed-care plans as a value-added benefit, or a state RHTP subaward. Consumer self-pay of $349 to $699. Employer add-on for rural self-insured plans. Margin on lodging and rides.
non_obvious_insight: When a unit closes, the hospital's cost disappears and the family's cost explodes in the final three weeks. The fix is logistics (room blocks, dispatch, triage), which a non-clinical startup can assemble in weeks. Medicaid finances roughly four in ten US births and already pays for non-emergency transport, so the payer exists. The wedge is packaging this as a contractable benefit plans can add, with roadside-birth and ED-bypass metrics as proof.
first_30_days: Pick one closure county in the news and its receiving hospital 45 to 90 minutes away. Contract 6 discounted extended-stay rooms, one local transport operator and a telehealth OB-nurse line. Pilot with 20 mothers via the county health department, WIC and rural clinics, priced at cost or free. Log outcomes. Pitch two Medicaid plans' value-added-benefit teams and the state RHTP office with the pilot data and a one-page subaward proposal before the October 30 obligation deadline. In parallel, sell the consumer version through rural parenting groups, churches and doulas.

title: Neutral Baselines and Neighbor Guarantees for Data Centers
one_liner: A neutral third party installs pre-construction sensors around proposed data centers and administers a developer-funded, automatic payout guarantee to neighbors, so permit fights run on evidence.
customer: Independent and mid-size data center developers seeking 50-500 MW campus approvals in contested counties. County commissions and state regulators are a second buyer because they can make the service a permit condition. Hyperscalers with in-house community teams are not the target.
problem: Permit fights are evidence-poor. Nobody has a pre-construction baseline of well levels, night-time noise, air quality or voltage at homes, so every later complaint about dry wells or a hum can be neither proven nor disproven. Both sides fight on feelings and lawyers. Politics has turned: New York paused environmental permits for data centers of 50 MW or more in July 2026, Texas ordered its environmental regulator to stop issuing new data center permits in September 2026, and local pauses now exist in at least 14 states. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found only 14% of Americans would welcome one nearby.
solution: Baseline-in-a-Box. Over 60-90 days before the application, deploy 30-60 low-cost sensors: property-line night noise, depth and conductivity in volunteer neighbors' wells, PM2.5, night-sky brightness, and voltage sag at homes. Publish a read-only public dashboard. Have a university extension hydrogeologist and an acoustician review the methods. Escrow the data with hash-anchored timestamps so neither side can edit it. Keep monitoring for 10 years. Then add a Neighbor Guarantee: a developer-funded escrow that pays affected households automatically, like parametric crop insurance, when verified well drawdown or noise exceedances occur. No lawsuit is needed.
why_now: In 2026 the moratorium movement jumped from town boards to governors' offices (New York's executive order of July 14, Texas's TCEQ permit halt of September 21). Developers now need social license as much as megawatts, and regulators are actively drafting the frameworks that will say what evidence counts.
revenue_model: The developer pays $75-150k per site for setup, $4-10k per month for monitoring, and an 8-10% administration fee on the guarantee escrow. Counties that write the service into permit conditions create repeat demand. Later, anonymized data licensing to regulators and insurers.
non_obvious_insight: The baseline protects the developer more than the opponents. It is the only defense against future exaggerated or mistaken claims, and it turns 'trust us' into 'audit us'. Parametric payouts replace adversarial claims, which is why a rational developer buys it from a neutral party rather than opposing it.
first_30_days: Pick one county with a pending rezoning hearing (Georgia, Virginia, Indiana, Pennsylvania or Texas). Offer the developer's land agent a free 30-day pilot on 10 neighbor wells with an agricultural-extension partner. Build nodes from off-the-shelf parts at about $1.5-3k each. Present the live dashboard at the public hearing and convert that developer to a paid contract. Use the result as the case study for the next 5 developers.

title: Pay-Per-Attendance Social Prescriptions for Loneliness
one_liner: A settlement layer where health systems and employers pay small local groups (Men's Sheds, choirs, walking clubs) a fixed fee for every verified attendance by a doctor-referred lonely patient.
customer: Nonprofit-hospital community-benefit and population-health teams and self-insured employers first, then Medicare Advantage plans. The suppliers who get paid are local groups: Men's Sheds, choirs, run and walking clubs, craft circles.
problem: Social prescribing works abroad (Merton, London: GP visits down 33%, A&E visits down 50%) and WHO now attributes about 871k deaths a year to isolation. The US has no reimbursement path, so PCPs with 31-day waits have nowhere to send lonely patients. Third places run on volunteers and charity, and referral directories list them without paying them. Loneliness programs fail on retention, because people stop showing up after week 2.
solution: Screen for loneliness in primary care or at employer open enrollment (UCLA-3 or a similar short scale). The clinician sends an e-referral to a vetted local group, and the patient checks in by QR or NFC at each session. The buyer pays the group $8-15 per verified attendance, capped per member per month, and the platform keeps 15-20%. A dashboard tracks show rate at weeks 4 and 8, loneliness score change and ED or visit utilization. It is a payment and verification rail, not a social network. Groups are paid to be welcoming and to keep people coming, which is the opposite of an engagement-maximizing app.
why_now: WHO's June 2025 Commission report made loneliness a measured global health metric. Dating and social apps are stalling (Bumble layoffs, BFF relaunch), so friendship demand has no monetized supply. Medicaid work requirements from Jan 2027 and lapsed ACA subsidies are squeezing hospital margins and pushing systems toward cheap prevention with measurable ROI. Employers are also cutting expensive drug benefits and looking for low-cost wellbeing spend.
revenue_model: Per-verified-attendance settlement (buyer pays, group gets about 80-85%), plus a small PMPM or annual platform fee for the outcome dashboard and clinic workflow. Later, Medicare Advantage supplemental-benefit contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not loneliness interventions. It is a business model for the hosts. A health payer already pays 10-100x $10 per avoided ED visit, and paying per attendance turns retention (the real failure point) into the unit of revenue. Referral directories like Findhelp route people but do not pay, and hosts cannot survive on referrals alone.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 small groups in one metro and sign each to a $10-per-attendance pilot. Sign one health-system community-benefit office or one self-insured employer for 100 referrals. Build check-in with a QR code and a spreadsheet-backed dashboard, no app needed. Measure week-4 show rate against the roughly 20-30% typical of unpaid programs, then use that number to pitch the second buyer.

title: Tender-Time Snapshots: Post-Montgomery Broker Defense File
one_liner: A tamper-evident, per-load record of exactly what a broker knew about a carrier at the moment of tender, built to survive plaintiff discovery and to satisfy underwriters, then upgraded into a placed contingent-liability program for small brokers.
customer: Independent brokerages and host-agency networks doing roughly $2M-$60M in gross revenue that buy contingent auto liability through a wholesaler. Secondary payers: MGAs, wholesalers and E&S carriers that now need underwriting evidence.
problem: On May 14, 2026 the Supreme Court unanimously held in Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II that negligent-hiring claims against brokers are not preempted by the FAAAA, so state-law suits now reach discovery. Insurance trade press (The Insurer, Sept 17, 2026, quoting RPS) is already calling it a capacity problem for broker contingent liability, and underwriters are asking for a paper trail of what was reviewed, when, and what was concluded. A small broker's carrier file is an onboarding PDF from 14 months ago plus email threads. Authority status, insurance, safety rating, ownership and contact info can change any day, and nobody can show what the screen said on the day of the load.
solution: Hook into tender events (TMS export, rate-con email forward, or load-board booking). At each tender, pull and hash-timestamp a snapshot: authority status, safety rating, insurance certificate validity, CSA/out-of-service rates, recent MCS-150 or contact-info changes, fraud flags, and which of the broker's own written selection rules the carrier passed. Any override is logged with a reason and the person who made it. A one-click 'selection file' export is formatted for a discovery request. Ship templates for a written carrier-selection standard drafted with trucking defense counsel. Phase 2: use the aggregated data to place small brokers into a wholesaler/MGA contingent-liability program with pricing credit for documented behavior.
why_now: Montgomery (May 14, 2026) removed the broad preemption defense. Contingent auto liability and E&O are repricing and capacity is tightening, per industry reporting in Sept 2026. The FMCSA broker financial-responsibility rule took full effect Jan 16, 2026, with suspension if security stays below $75K for 7 business days, so brokers cannot absorb a surprise verdict or claim.
revenue_model: SaaS at $0.50-$1.50 per tendered load or $300-$1,200/month by volume. Phase 2 adds a 10-15% commission on premium placed through the program, plus referral fees from defense firms.
non_obvious_insight: Plaintiffs' counsel does not ask 'did you vet the carrier?' They ask 'show me what your system showed at the minute you tendered, and who overrode it.' Brokers who vetted diligently at onboarding still lose, because they cannot prove tender-day state. Every broker knows the overrides happen at 4:45pm on a Friday when a load must be covered, and underwriters will price that override discipline. The record also proves the absence of red flags, which is the reasonable-care defense.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 small brokers through freight-broker Facebook groups and TIA chapters. Co-write a reasonable-care checklist with one trucking defense attorney. Build a snapshot logger on public FMCSA data plus an insurance-certificate check, ingesting tenders by CSV or forwarded rate-con emails so no TMS integration is needed. The sales hook is a free 'Discovery Fire Drill': simulate a plaintiff's request against the broker's last 5 loads and show the gaps. Convert at $299/month. In parallel, take the aggregate data to two wholesale brokers to test whether a premium credit is feasible.

title: Managed 24-Hour CRA Vulnerability Reporting Desk
one_liner: A hosted OWASP Dependency-Track plus an on-call analyst rota that tells small hardware makers within hours whether an exploited vulnerability hits their firmware, then drafts the ENISA 24h/72h filings.
customer: EU-selling makers of connected hardware with 5-250 staff and no product-security team (smart-home devices, e-bikes, EV chargers, industrial gateways, toys, wearables). Buyer is the CTO or regulatory/CE-marking manager. Secondary channel is CE-marking consultants who need a white-label reporting partner.
problem: The EU Cyber Resilience Act's reporting duties went live on 11 Sept 2026. Manufacturers must send an early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability, then detail within 72 hours, through ENISA's Single Reporting Platform. Fines reach EUR 15M or 2.5% of turnover. Small makers ship Yocto, OpenWrt, Zephyr, OpenSSL and FFmpeg stacks and often can't say what is inside a firmware image. Nobody on their team is awake on Sunday when a CISA KEV entry lands.
solution: Ingest CycloneDX/SPDX SBOMs into a managed Dependency-Track instance. For products with no SBOM, generate one from the firmware image with Syft, cdxgen or EMBA, using Ghidra for binary-only blobs. Watch CISA KEV, the EU vulnerability database and OSV continuously. A human analyst issues a VEX verdict (affected / not affected / under investigation) within hours. If affected, the desk pre-fills the SRP notification, drafts the customer advisory, and tracks the 24h, 72h and final-report clocks. The output is an auditable VEX history that a market-surveillance authority or notified body can read.
why_now: The 24-hour reporting clock started 11 Sept 2026 and the ENISA platform is open, so thousands of small makers are discovering they have weeks rather than the Dec 2027 date for full application. Dependency-Track and CycloneDX are the de facto open standards, but the paid options are enterprise appsec suites priced far above a 20-person hardware company's budget.
revenue_model: Retainer of EUR 300-1,500 per month per product family, tiered by number of firmware images and response-time SLA. One-off firmware SBOM generation at EUR 2-8k per image. Resale to CE consultants at a wholesale rate. Later add annual CRA technical-file support.
non_obvious_insight: Small manufacturers don't need another scanner, because the open-source plumbing already works. They need a human who can say 'not affected' with evidence inside 24 hours, because a false 'affected' filing is also costly. The scarce asset is analyst judgment plus a growing VEX history, which compounds across customers who share the same upstream components.
first_30_days: Stand up stock Dependency-Track and a KEV/EUVD watcher. Recruit 2-3 freelance embedded-security engineers for a shared on-call rota. Offer 20 free 'CRA exposure scans' (one firmware image in, one-page exposed-CVE report out) to IoT startups and to 100 CE-marking consultants found on LinkedIn and trade forums. Publish a weekly 'which exploited CVEs hit your Yocto/OpenWrt image' digest to build the list. Convert scans into 6-month retainers at a design-partner price.

title: Failed-Part Bounty for Insurance Subrogation
one_liner: Pay plumbers a bounty to bag, photograph and chain-of-custody the pipe, supply line or fitting that failed, then sell the evidence and a brand-level failure database to insurers' subrogation units and manufacturers.
customer: Subrogation departments and subro vendors at regional and mutual homeowners insurers (the ones too small to send a forensic engineer to a $9k supply-line loss). Second buyers: plumbing manufacturers, distributors and private-label buyers who license the failure data.
problem: Water damage is among the top two homeowner claim categories. Product-defect subrogation (a supply line, PEX fitting, toilet connector, ice-maker line or water heater that failed early) only works if someone kept the failed part. The plumber is on scene 1 to 3 days before the adjuster, cuts the failed piece out, and tosses it in the truck-bed scrap bin. When the adjuster arrives the evidence is gone, the insurer eats the loss, and the manufacturer's lawyers cite spoliation. Insurers only hire the $2,000 forensic engineer on the big losses, so the routine $8-15k losses are never pursued. Meanwhile every plumber knows which brands are failing (certain plastic-nut braided lines, certain fill valves, certain fitting lots) but nobody aggregates it.
solution: A 90-second protocol and kit. Tamper-evident bag with a QR label, a phone flow (photo of the part in place, photo after removal, the manufacturer stamp or date code, homeowner e-signature by text, and the claim number if one exists). A weekly courier pickup from the shop and a climate-controlled evidence locker. Optional one-page factual cause-of-loss statement drawn from the same photos (sudden burst versus long-term seepage, which is exactly the 'gradual leak' exclusion that decides whether homeowners get paid). Every part is logged by brand, model, date code and failure mode, which builds a Backblaze-style public failure-rate report by product line. Insurers get the part plus a ready evidence package. The shop gets a bounty and a small line item on the invoice.
why_now: Water-loss severity has risen sharply and carriers are under pressure on homeowners loss ratios, so they are hunting for recovery dollars. Copper and steel tariffs plus the shift to PEX and imported fittings have flooded the market with cheaper components of unknown quality. Photo and OCR tooling now makes a cheap, standardized evidence workflow possible, and the subrogation trade press is openly saying evidence preservation is the make-or-break step.
revenue_model: Insurer or subro vendor pays $75-150 per part with a documented chain of custody, of which $40-60 goes to the shop and tech. Plus a 3-8% success share on any recovery that follows. Plus annual data licenses ($15-60k) to manufacturers, distributors and big-box private-label buyers, and per-report fees for expert-witness-ready packages.
non_obvious_insight: The evidence that decides tens of millions in recoveries is currently destroyed daily by the only people who touch it first, and the reason is not malice. Nobody pays a tech to spend 4 minutes and a bag on a piece of scrap. The plumber, not the adjuster, is the true first-notice-of-loss for the product itself. The bounty is a price signal, and the dataset that falls out is one nobody else can buy.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 shops through a local PHCC chapter and the owner Facebook and peer groups with a flat $50 per bag and a free kit. Design the label and the phone flow in a form tool. Collect the first 50 parts with photos. Take the first 20 case files to two regional mutual insurers and a subrogation vendor and ask them which they would have pursued. Sell a paid pilot for 100 parts on the strength of their answers.

title: Tariff Surcharge Credit-Memo Recovery for Mid-Size Manufacturers
one_liner: Mine a plant's accounts-payable history for 2025-26 tariff surcharges, then win credit memos from the distributors who are now receiving IEEPA refunds.
customer: US manufacturers with $5M-$200M revenue and 30-300 active vendors who paid line-item 'tariff surcharges' or tariff-justified price increases from March 2025 through the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling. The buyer is the CFO, controller or purchasing director.
problem: Refunds go to the importer of record, and importers of record are usually distributors: fastener houses, bearing and fitting suppliers, steel service centers, electronics distributors, tooling vendors. The plant paid the surcharge but has no claim with CBP. Downstream buyers have to rely on contract and unjust-enrichment theories against the vendor. Large retailers have law firms doing this, but a $4k-$60k claim per vendor is below any law firm's floor. Plant managers also will not sue the only source of a hydraulic fitting, so the claims are simply going unasked.
solution: 'SurchargeScan': connect to QuickBooks, NetSuite, Epicor or Infor (or upload AP PDFs). AI extracts surcharge lines and tariff-justified price-increase letters, ranks vendors by likelihood of being the importer of record (using public bill-of-lading data and vendor type), and generates reservation-of-rights letters. It then runs a relationship-preserving negotiation for credit memos against future orders instead of cash demands, and tracks each vendor's refund status through CBP's CAPE process. A partner law firm signs off on letters and escalates only large or hostile cases.
why_now: The Supreme Court held the IEEPA tariffs unlawful in February 2026. CBP launched its CAPE refund module on April 20, 2026, with well over $100B accepted for processing. The government is appealing the Court of International Trade's refund order, so vendors are receiving cash now while uncertainty still gives buyers leverage. Every month vendors book the windfall as profit, the claim gets harder to recover.
revenue_model: 20%-25% contingency on recovered credits and cash, plus a $499 scan fee credited against the fee. Average expected recovery of $25k-$150k per plant, with margins on a heavily automated flow. Later, an ongoing 'duty-pass-through audit' for any future tariff regime.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody in the surcharge fight wants to be in court with their own supplier. Plant managers will happily take a credit memo on the next PO but will never file a lawsuit, so the winning product is a diplomatic credit negotiation run by software, not a demand-letter factory.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 Ohio plant controllers as design partners with a free scan in return for 20% on recoveries. Build the scanner with an LLM over exported AP data plus a public bill-of-lading lookup. Send 20 reservation-of-rights letters and get the first credit memos booked. Sign a referral and review agreement with one trade-law boutique. Publish the recovery rate data from the first 10 vendors to sell the next 50 plants.

title: Enclave Escrow: Buy Data by Measured Lift
one_liner: A confidential-compute clean room where the buyer's evaluation runs on the seller's data inside an attested enclave, and the price is set by the measured lift, so neither side reveals its asset before agreeing.
customer: Quant funds, ML teams and R&D groups buying alternative or proprietary datasets, and the small data sellers (satellite counts, AIS ship data, web panels, lab datasets) who cannot afford NDAs and legal cycles. Autonomous buyer agents are the growth channel.
problem: Arrow's information paradox: you cannot value data without seeing it, but once you see it you do not need to buy it. Sellers therefore refuse trials or overprice, buyers waste budget on blind purchases, and agents purchasing autonomously cannot sign NDAs or judge value.
solution: Seller uploads an encrypted dataset. Buyer uploads a hashed evaluation harness (a backtest, a fine-tune validation run, an accuracy test). Both run inside a CPU plus GPU trusted execution environment with remote attestation. Only a signed lift score leaves the enclave, under a per-pair query budget or differential-privacy noise to stop the score being used as an extraction oracle. A pre-agreed schedule converts lift into a license price, and payment triggers automatically if the buyer opts in.
why_now: Confidential computing on Hopper and Blackwell GPUs now runs with little performance penalty and produces GPU-signed attestation reports. Cloud providers and GPU-TEE clouds sell it off the shelf. Agents with pay-per-request data endpoints are starting to buy data blind.
revenue_model: 5-10% of transaction value, compute pass-through, $5-25k per paid evaluation for funds, and a subscription for private clean rooms.
non_obvious_insight: Sell the measurement, not the data. The thing placed in escrow is an experiment both sides commit to before seeing the result, which turns the sale into outcome-linked pricing and lets tiny sellers with no legal team participate. Bounding the lift oracle (query budgets) is the hard, defensible engineering piece.
first_30_days: Sign 3 small alt-data sellers and 2 small funds or ML teams for paid pilots. Use rented confidential VMs and a manually built harness for each evaluation. Charge $5k per evaluation and deliver a signed report. Use results to write a public 'pay for lift' pricing template.

title: Presence Ledger: Reconstruct Every Trip You Took
one_liner: Ingests flight emails, CBP I-94 history, location exports and passport stamps to produce an evidence-backed, officer-proof travel table for naturalization, green-card retention and tax residency.
customer: Immigration law firms (per-client fee), CPAs and tax preparers serving foreign nationals (Form 8843/substantial presence test), HR mobility teams, and green card holders or naturalization applicants directly.
problem: N-400 applicants must list every trip of 24 hours or more in the past 5 years with exact dates. Almost no one can. Officers compare the list with CBP entry and exit records, and an honest gap or mismatch turns an interview into a good-moral-character or false-testimony problem. Green card holders with long absences risk a presumption of broken continuous residence, and scrutiny of returning residents at ports of entry has risen. The same reconstruction is needed for IRS substantial presence day counts, state tax residency audits, and Schengen/UK day counts. Paralegals spend 1-3 hours per client pulling this together by hand, and it is still wrong.
solution: A consent-based tool that pulls the official CBP I-94 travel history, scans Gmail/Outlook for airline and hotel confirmations, ingests Google Timeline or phone location exports and card transactions, and OCRs photos of passport stamps. It reconciles them into a single timeline with confidence flags, asks the user only about unresolved gaps, and exports (a) an N-400-style trip table with the proof behind each row, (b) day counts for physical presence, substantial presence and Schengen limits, and (c) a warning when a planned trip would cross a risk threshold (for example 180 days, or a trip that would break continuous residence).
why_now: Naturalization is being scrutinized more heavily in 2025-26, with a new civics test, a renewed focus on good moral character and reinstated neighborhood-style inquiries. Border stops of returning residents are up. Remote and hybrid work has multiplied cross-border days and tax exposure. Location data is now easy to export from phones, and LLMs make email and stamp parsing cheap enough for a small team to build in weeks.
revenue_model: $49-79 per case billed to law firms (white-label), $29-49 self-serve for applicants, $12-20 per client for CPAs during tax season, and a $9/month subscription for green card holders who want ongoing day tracking and pre-trip risk checks.
non_obvious_insight: The danger is not the trips you forget but the mismatch between your list and what the government already holds. A trip table with attached proof, pre-reconciled against CBP's own record, changes the tone of an interview. The exact same dataset is what tax audits and residency disputes need, so an immigration wedge opens a much larger tax-residency market with no extra data collection.
first_30_days: Build only the N-400 5-year trip table with I-94 history import plus email parsing. Give it free to 10 immigration firms in exchange for a testimonial and a comparison against their manual tables. Charge $49 from client number 11 on. Post the before/after error rates from real cases. In parallel, offer a $15 8843/substantial-presence day-count report through 5 CPAs who serve OPT/H-1B clients.

title: Cask Audit: Proof of Existence for Whisky Investors
one_liner: An independent inspection, gauging and valuation service that verifies investor-owned whisky casks exist, contain what was sold, and are worth what the seller says.
customer: Retail cask investors, IFAs and wealth managers, insolvency practitioners and law firms, and honest cask brokers who want a trust seal.
problem: The cask market has been in a glut since 2022 (auction surplus, distillery consolidation, lower price per litre) and has documented fraud cases where audits found casks missing or filled with substandard spirit. Investors cannot verify holdings or exit.
solution: Field inspectors in bonded warehouses attest existence, fill level, strength, cask type and warehouse-receipt ownership, with geotagged photos. Quarterly valuations use bottling yield and market comps, and brokers pay to join an 'audited cask' registry.
why_now: In a downturn demand shifts from buying more to proving what you own. Fraud taints every honest broker, so third-party proof is worth paying for.
revenue_model: GBP 150-300 per cask audit, broker subscriptions for continuous audit, and valuation reports.
non_obvious_insight: Bonded-warehouse access is already a contractual owner right, so inspectors are cheap to deploy, while buyers of proof are motivated by loss and by seller reputation. The bourbon cask market is a later expansion. Confirm warehouse cooperation and local regulation early.
first_30_days: Recruit 2 warehouse-keepers, audit 30 casks for 10 investors at a GBP 100 pilot rate, publish anonymized findings, and approach IFAs and insolvency firms.

title: Regulator-Grade Black Box for Collections Voice Agents
one_liner: A vendor-neutral audit layer that records, checks and attests every AI collections call so lenders can prove the bot behaved.
customer: Mid-size Indian NBFCs, microfinance institutions, digital lenders and collection BPOs running voice AI (Mahindra Finance alone runs about 10M AI calls across 12 languages). The voice-AI vendors selling to them are a channel partner.
problem: Regulators penalize the lender, not the software vendor, for harassment, off-hours calls (RBI allows recovery contact roughly 8am-7pm), third-party contact and false promises. A hallucinated 'your loan is waived' or a threatening tone is a compliance event. No human team can audit millions of calls in 12 languages. Household debt stress is rising (Indonesia paylater defaults, Brazil 82% household-debt indicator), so collection volume and scrutiny are both increasing.
solution: A third-party layer that ingests call audio or streams, runs in-language policy checks (hours, DND and consent status, forbidden phrases, promise-making, tone) and writes a hash-chained call ledger. Native-speaker reviewers sample 1-3% of flagged calls. Each month it issues a regulator-ready attestation pack with violation rates by vendor and script version. Lenders can gate scripts or vendors on the scores, and insurers of the vendors can use the same pack.
why_now: Indian voice-AI orchestration has exploded (Ringg, Bolna, Gnani, Blue Machines) and lenders now run millions of AI calls. ISO's gen-AI exclusions and Verisk's agentic exclusions are pushing carriers to demand evidence before covering AI conduct. Rising defaults in Indonesia and Brazil mean the same product exports.
revenue_model: Per-call-minute fee (roughly Rs 0.10-0.30) or annual attestation subscription of Rs 15-50 lakh per lender, plus a reseller margin through voice-AI vendors.
non_obvious_insight: The vendor can never be its own auditor, and the buyer's budget comes from penalty avoidance, not from a tech line. That makes this a compliance-assurance purchase like a statutory audit, which is stickier and higher-priced than a monitoring dashboard. Whoever becomes the accepted attestor also becomes the data source insurers price from.
first_30_days: Offer a free retrospective audit of 10,000 already-recorded calls to three NBFCs or collection BPOs. Build it on open ASR plus a rules library in Hindi, Marathi and Tamil, with two native reviewers. Deliver a violations report to the chief compliance officer, then convert to a monthly attestation contract.

title: Friday Programs for Four-Day School Districts
one_liner: A turnkey 'fifth-day' care and enrichment operator that runs in existing school buildings for districts on four-day weeks, funded by parent fees and vouchers.
customer: Rural and small-town districts on four-day weeks (hundreds of districts across 20+ states, from memory) and their working parents. Also 21st CCLC and state after-school grant programs.
problem: Districts adopted four-day weeks to cut costs and recruit teachers. The off day leaves working parents with no care in places where licensed slots are already scarce, so kids stay alone, with grandparents or parents leave jobs. Each district improvises its own Friday program.
solution: An operating kit: a staffing pool (education majors and retired teachers), background-check pipeline, daily curriculum, parent sign-up and payment, subsidy-voucher billing, insurance and transport. The district provides the building. We run the first sites ourselves, then license the kit for a management fee.
why_now: ESSER money ended, so more districts are trimming days (from memory). Childcare prices are up 29% since 2020 and rural supply is thin. CCDF rules moving to enrollment-based payment help small operators get paid reliably.
revenue_model: Parent fee of $35-50 per child per day, with a 15% management fee or per-site licence when franchised to local operators. Voucher billing adds funded slots.
non_obvious_insight: This desert is a day-of-week desert created by a policy choice, and the most expensive input (the building) is already paid for by taxpayers. That makes the unit economics better than standard childcare.
first_30_days: Call 20 four-day-week districts in Missouri, Oklahoma and Colorado. Run one paid pilot Friday with 15-25 kids at $40 a day. Recruit staff from the nearest college's education program. Track true margin per child-day and use the data to sell the second district.

title: Hard-Alloy Print Recipes via Sample-Efficient AI Campaigns
one_liner: Sell validated 3D-print parameter recipes and 40-build AI-guided optimization campaigns so ordinary mid-power metal printers can make alloys that normally need rare high-power machines.
customer: Metal additive-manufacturing job shops and small rocket, space and defense suppliers with 400-500 W class printers. University AM labs are a secondary buyer.
problem: GRCop-42, a copper-chromium-niobium rocket-engine alloy, is hard and costly to print. It typically needs high laser power, and about 90% of commercial printers cannot handle it. Every failed build wastes powder and machine time, and shops cannot afford months of trial and error.
solution: A recipe library of machine-specific, validated parameter sets and build reports, sold per alloy and per machine model. It comes with a paid 'campaign' service that uses Bayesian or active-learning search to find working settings in about 40 builds from a few failed starting points. Customer builds feed back into the shared library.
why_now: Washington State University's team used AI to search over 100 million candidate settings, started from 37 failed experiments, and found 6 successful settings in 40 experiments over 3 months, including a first successful print at a record-low 500 W. The work won an Innovative Deployed Application Award, and active-learning frameworks for science are appearing on arXiv (for example arXiv:2609.31197). The method is proven and unlicensed to shops.
revenue_model: Recipe licenses at roughly $5-30k per alloy-machine pair, campaign fees of roughly $20-60k, and an annual recipe-library subscription for shops.
non_obvious_insight: The product is not the alloy but the experiment budget. The WSU study says 90% of commercial printers cannot print GRCop-42 and that success required 'a very challenging case for AI' with rare successes, and the lead author says they are 'essentially democratizing the printing' of the alloy (https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/08/260827010504.htm). Selling failure-avoidance to shops that cannot afford 37 failed builds is a service business, not a materials business.
first_30_days: Contact the WSU authors and WSU's commercialization office about licensing the method. Recruit 2-3 job shops with 400-500 W machines and quote a fixed-price GRCop-42 campaign, with the shop supplying powder and machine time. Pre-sell the first recipe pack to rocket and space startups. Run the first campaign in month 2 and publish a build-report case study.

title: Tariff Exposure Radar by House Plan
one_liner: A per-plan bill-of-materials scan that flags the small imported, tariff-exposed slice of inputs, prices the swing and proposes lower-exposure substitutes.
customer: Purchasing managers and owners at regional and mid-size builders (100-2,000 homes a year), remodelers, and building-material dealers. Distribution via home builders associations.
problem: NAHB estimates tariffs add $10,900 per home and Brookings sees about $30B added to residential construction and renovation cost by 2027. Only about 7% of inputs are imported, but they are mostly items with no quick domestic substitute, and reported lumber and steel tariff rates conflict across sources. Builders reprice by gut, sign fixed-price contracts blind, and have no per-plan exposure number.
solution: Ingest plan takeoffs and supplier price lists, map each SKU to country of origin and tariff line, and compute exposure per plan and per option package. Deliver escalation-clause language for buyer and sub contracts, alerts when rates change, substitute suggestions from domestic or alternate-origin catalogs, and a group-buy on substitutes.
why_now: Tariff rates are moving and sources disagree. Builder margins are gone (63% use incentives), so a $10K per-home swing decides whether a plan pencils. Structured plan data is now available from design-automation tools.
revenue_model: $500-2,000 per month per builder. $1,500 one-off plan audits. 2-4% rebate on substituted spend from group buys.
non_obvious_insight: Because most of a house is domestic, the tariff burden is a short list of SKUs, so the right tool is a narrow, boring lookup rather than a global trade-compliance platform. The money is in plan-level re-spec and escalation clauses, not in customs filings.
first_30_days: Offer 10 builders a free top-40 exposed-SKU audit from their last three takeoffs and supplier quotes. Send a one-page report and convert 3 to paid. Get a slot in a regional builders association newsletter.

title: Shelved-Game Rescue Exchange
one_liner: A broker that packages cancelled and orphaned game prototypes and licenses them to laid-off veteran teams on revenue-share terms, with reversion rights if the game stalls.
customer: Publishers, closing studios and insolvency administrators holding unreleased builds (they get a recovery instead of a write-off). The paying counterparties are veteran-led small teams and the funders behind them.
problem: Ubisoft cancelled six games in Jan 2026 and cut headcount from 18,666 to 16,590. EA's owners closed a $55B LBO with $20B of debt and a stated plan to cut costs with AI. Cancelled projects sit unused with teams disbanded, while laid-off veterans have skills but no IP or prototype budget.
solution: Build a 'prototype data room' per project: build, design docs, and a third-party licence and music clearance audit. Add a standard rescue licence (revenue share, milestone reversion, credit terms) and a registry of veteran team leads. Match the two, and offer milestone-funded finishing through a small fund or partner investors. Start with insolvent and small publishers, which move faster than Ubisoft or EA legal.
why_now: The 2023-26 layoff wave left an unusually deep bench of finished-quality talent. The EA LBO and Ubisoft restructuring guarantee more shelved work. Steam distribution and Epic's 0% fee on the first $1M make a 10-20 person finish economically viable.
revenue_model: 10-15% of the licensee's revenue share, or a success fee at signing ($10-50k), plus a data-room packaging fee paid by the rights holder.
non_obvious_insight: A shelved game's cost to its owner is legal and opportunity overhead, not the code. A zero-upfront licence with reversion beats a write-down and avoids a public fire sale. Insiders assume cancelled means bad, but many projects die for portfolio or budget-cycle reasons, not quality.
first_30_days: Publish a public 'orphaned prototypes wanted' page. Call 20 insolvency administrators and mid-size publishers found through recent studio-closure announcements with a one-page offer. Have a games lawyer draft the rescue licence. Recruit 10 veteran-led teams from layoff communities on Discord and LinkedIn. Aim for one signed rescue by day 60.

title: Lake Ice Posts for Ice-Fishing Resorts
one_liner: Cheap solar LoRa thermistor-chain posts frozen into lake ice along access routes, giving resort operators and snowmobile clubs a live thickness trend and rate-of-change alerts on a seasonal subscription.
customer: Ice-fishing resorts and outfitters that rent ice houses and plow ice roads (Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, New York, Maine, Ontario), snowmobile clubs that groom lake trails, ice-derby and tournament organizers, lake associations and rescue units.
problem: Ice thickness varies across a lake and changes fast with warm rain, currents and springs. Resorts rely on daily manual auger checks at a few points. Vehicle and ice-house losses, and deaths, happen. Recent low-ice winters make timing harder. Research-grade buoys exist but cost far too much for a resort, and crowdsourced apps can't watch one specific corridor.
solution: A roughly USD 150 solar post with a thermistor chain spanning air, ice and water, plus a tilt sensor. It infers ice thickness from the 0 degree C interface and gradient, calibrated against the operator's own auger readings. Deploy 3-6 posts along the access road and ice-house village. The dashboard uses plain thresholds by vehicle class, texts an alert on rapid thinning, and offers an embeddable public 'ice conditions' widget for the resort's website.
why_now: It is late September, so units built now can be frozen in for this winter's first ice. LoRa, solar and thermistor chains are commodity. Ice-data apps (satellite radar, crowd reports) prove operators will pay for information, and research-grade buoys have validated the concept, leaving a low-cost tier open.
revenue_model: USD 199 hardware, plus USD 99-249 per post per season. Resort bundle of USD 1,500-4,000 per season. Sponsorship of the public widget by bait shops and outdoor brands. Contract work for counties and rescue units.
non_obvious_insight: Don't sell 'is the ice safe,' which is uncertifiable and a liability trap. Sell operational due diligence and a rate-of-change early warning: ice fails by trend (thermal decay, current), and a fixed post sees the trend before a weekly auger check does. Resorts lose money and reputation when they close roads early or lose a vehicle, so revenue protection is the wedge.
first_30_days: Build 25 posts before first freeze from off-the-shelf thermistor strings, LoRa boards and small solar panels. Sign 4-5 resorts to shoulder-season pilots at cost. Use their daily auger logs as ground truth. Launch a free public ice map to collect crowd calibration points and sponsors. Convert to season subscriptions and use winter data for next year's preorder round.

title: Break-Glass Interim Operators for Deceased Owners' Businesses
one_liner: An on-call bench of laid-off COOs and ops directors who step in within 48 hours when the sole owner of a small business dies, keeping it alive until the heirs can sell or close it.
customer: Estate attorneys, CPAs, SBA lenders and key-person insurers who need the business to keep its value, plus the widow or heirs. The estate ultimately pays from business cash flow or sale proceeds. Target businesses: HVAC and trades firms, machine shops, independent insurance agencies, restaurants and other 5-50 employee owner-dependent companies.
problem: Probate treats assets as inert (houses, accounts), but a running business melts within 90 days when the owner dies: bank signing authority, payroll, licenses, customer relationships and key employees all hinge on one person. Executors are grieving family. Attorneys cannot run a company. Brokers cannot sell one in freefall. Boomers still own a large share of employer businesses, so this is a huge, mostly invisible transfer.
solution: A vetted bench of interim managers with a 72-hour playbook: secure bank and payroll access via letters testamentary or a special administrator, notify customers and vendors, fund key-employee retention from the estate, arrange licensing 'qualifier' coverage where required, stabilize for 60-90 days, prep a data room, then hand off to a broker or buyer. AI tools (contract abstraction, bookkeeping analysis, KPI dashboards) let a newcomer understand the business in about a week. Owners can pre-buy a 'continuity plan' retainer.
why_now: The largest generational transfer of small businesses is under way (Cerulli: $124T through 2048, about 81% from Boomers and older), while the 2026 labor market is full of experienced ops leaders who cannot find roles. Cheap AI document and finance tooling makes fast onboarding of an unfamiliar business feasible for the first time.
revenue_model: Interim GM day rate of $900-1,500 billed to the estate, with the bench member keeping about 65%. Pre-need continuity retainer of about $1,200/yr for solo owners. Success fee on a sale, in coordination with brokers.
non_obvious_insight: The estate needs a verb, not a noun. The legal system has a process for distributing what a person owned but none for continuing what a person did. Unemployed senior operators are the perfect supply for that verb, and their downside is only the awkwardness of arriving during grief.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 laid-off ops and finance leaders. Write the 72-hour playbook. Offer a free 'owner-death readiness check' at bar association and CPA society events for 30 attorneys and accountants. Sell a $1,200/yr continuity retainer to 20 solo-owner businesses through one insurance agency or SBA lender's client list. The first at-need engagements will come from those attorneys' existing clients.

title: Wearable-Triggered Spending Guardrails for Sports Bettors
one_liner: A debit card and betting-budget wallet that tightens gambling, day-trading and BNPL limits automatically when the wearer's sleep, heart-rate variability and late-night pattern predict impulsive decisions, with an optional spouse or sponsor as co-guardian.
customer: US adults who bet legally on sports or prediction markets and want limits: self-referred users, partners and recovery groups first. Credit unions and employer assistance programs are the B2B2C channel. The price is $6-9 a month.
problem: Roughly 40 states have legal sports betting and sports prediction contracts have spread. Household credit stress is at record levels, with delinquencies at highs and deposits often funded by cards or BNPL. Existing blocks are all-or-nothing, and willpower fails at 2 a.m. after a losing streak. A wearable knows when the user is depleted, but the bank has never seen that signal.
solution: An issued card and ledger, built on a card-issuing platform, that funds a weekly betting wallet. The user pre-commits the rules when calm. If sleep drops below a set threshold, HRV falls against baseline, or two late-night losses stack up, the wallet enters a 24-hour cooldown, cuts the daily cap, or asks a partner to approve top-ups. Wearable sync is opt-in via Oura, Whoop, Garmin or Apple Health. Only a one-bit cooldown flag leaves the phone.
why_now: Legal betting and prediction-market sports contracts scaled through 2025-26. Brazil banned online betting and announced debt relief on Sept 25, 2026, showing the politics have turned. The CFPB open-banking rule is stayed and unstable, so a business built on card-level controls avoids dependence on aggregator data. Wearables are now mainstream, with Whoop raising $575M this year.
revenue_model: $7 a month subscription plus interchange share. Credit unions and neobanks license it for $1-2 per member per month. State problem-gambling councils pay for evidence-based tools. Anything sold to sportsbooks is optional and kept separate to avoid conflicts.
non_obvious_insight: Financial products treat every hour as equal, but behavior is not. The best predictor of a regretted transaction is the user's physiological state at 1 a.m., which the user's own wearable measures and the bank never sees. Sell control, not surveillance: the user writes the rules in advance and a bank never sees raw health data.
first_30_days: Ship a no-card MVP: an SMS and Slack bot that uses the Oura or Whoop API to send cooldown alerts, plus a partner-approval flow. Recruit 50 users from recovering-bettor communities. Measure whether cooldowns cut after-midnight deposits. Then pilot with one credit union that already offers gambling merchant-category blocks, and price at $7 a month.

title: Grid-Paid Spiffs for Water Heater Installers
one_liner: Make the plumber on the emergency water-heater call the distribution channel for heat pump water heaters and grid demand-response programs, with a same-day rebate stack, an electrician handoff and a per-device bounty paid to the tech.
customer: Virtual power plant aggregators, utility demand-response and efficiency-program administrators and manufacturers' connected-water-heater programs, who pay for enrolled devices. The plumbing shop and tech are the paid channel partners.
problem: Roughly 9 million water heaters get replaced each year and the large majority are emergency replacements decided in a four-hour window, standing in an inch of water. The plumber decides what goes in. Utilities and aggregators spend hundreds of dollars per customer on mailers and rebates that almost nobody uses, because the customer does not think about the water heater until it dies. Plumbers install the 50-gallon tank on the truck because a heat pump unit needs a 240V circuit, a condensate drain, clearance and paperwork, plumbers do not do electrical, and a callback eats a week of margin. The federal 25C credit ended December 31, 2025, so what is left are state and utility rebates that customers cannot pre-approve while the old tank is leaking.
solution: An install-day tool for the tech's phone. Enter the ZIP, the current heater and a photo of the panel and get back every stackable rebate for that address with the homeowner's net cost against a like-for-like tank (a 20-second sales conversation). Route the 240V circuit to a pre-priced partner electrician for a next-day flat fee, or steer to a 120V plug-in heat pump model when the panel is tight. At install, scan the QR on the heater to enroll it in the aggregator or utility program with the customer's consent. Pay the tech a same-week spiff and the shop a fee. We handle rebate paperwork in the background so the plumber's job ends when the tank is set.
why_now: Federal tax credits are gone, so utility and state programs and point-of-sale rebates now decide the price difference. Virtual power plants and utility demand-response are actively looking for cheap, high-volume device enrollment. Manufacturers now ship connected and 120V plug-in heat pump units that remove the biggest install objections. The labor-constrained plumber has never been offered a spiff that is bigger than the hassle.
revenue_model: Take 20-30% of the per-device enrollment or midstream incentive paid by the aggregator or utility (typically $200-600 per device is now spent on customer acquisition), pay $50-100 to the tech and $50-100 to the shop, and keep the rest. Add a per-install electrician referral fee and a $99 per month shop subscription for the rebate engine once volumes justify it.
non_obvious_insight: The whole electrification industry markets to homeowners, who make no decision until the tank fails. The only person who actually decides is a plumber with a 20-minute window, paid by the ticket and hating callbacks. Plumbers will not sell a heat pump water heater because it is a worse day for them, not because they are anti-green. Fix the day and the channel opens, and the spiff is the cheapest customer acquisition the grid will ever buy.
first_30_days: Choose one territory with a live heat pump water heater rebate plus a demand-response or VPP program (e.g. Massachusetts, Colorado, the Pacific Northwest or California). Build the rebate stack for that utility in a spreadsheet and a text-message enrollment link. Sign 5 shops and 1 partner electrician. Pitch an aggregator or the program administrator a pilot of 100 enrolled devices at an agreed bounty, with the spiff paid manually at first.

title: Orphan Bin Network: Leased Farm Storage Capacity
one_liner: Lease the thousands of idle grain bins left on consolidated and inherited farmsteads, retrofit them with cheap sensors, and run them as licensed satellite storage for co-ops.
customer: Co-ops and independent elevators that run short of upright storage every big harvest. Also landlord and heir bin owners who receive lease income. The elevator pays a per-bin SaaS fee plus a share of storage revenue.
problem: Upright storage is the co-op's hardest constraint, and building new capacity costs a huge multiple of leasing existing steel. Ground piles cost shrink and quality. Meanwhile farm consolidation and aging landowners leave many bins idle on rented farmsteads. Heirs pay taxes on stranded assets and have no way to monetize them. Iowa law already contemplates leased storage facilities under a warehouse license (the licensee simply notifies the state), but no one has packaged the monitoring, inventory verification and paperwork to make it routine.
solution: A 'bin-in-a-box' program run under the co-op's existing warehouse license. Sign multi-year leases with owners and install a retrofit kit: temperature and moisture cables, fill-level sensors, aeration control and a remote camera. Wire it into the co-op's grain accounting system so receipts, inventory and shrink tracking work like any owned bin. Provide the compliance package (state notifications, insurance riders, inspection logs, an auditor-ready trail). This is not a marketplace. The co-op stays the licensed warehouseman and the bin owner becomes a landlord.
why_now: The 2025 record harvest left the top 12 corn states about 1.4 billion bushels short of upright storage, according to CoBank analysis, and low prices keep grain in storage longer. Elevators piled grain on the ground and rented temporary space. Cheap LoRa and cellular bin sensors now cost far less than a few years ago, and 2026 harvest is starting.
revenue_model: SaaS of about $250 to $500 per bin per year plus install margin on the sensor kit. 10% to 20% share of incremental storage revenue. Optional financing spread on kit costs.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not steel but licensed, monitored, insurable steel. Idle bins already exist by the thousands. What is missing is the trust layer (sensors, chain-of-custody and a bonded warehouseman) that lets an elevator sign for grain sitting in someone else's yard.
first_30_days: Pick one co-op that just piled grain on the ground. Identify 10 idle bins within 15 miles from the co-op's landlord and ag-lending contacts. Confirm the notification steps with the Iowa Grain Warehouse Bureau. Install sensor kits on 5 bins before harvest peak and store real grain for the first time this season.
